command.aerocore.sample.input: AeroCore sample: %s m/s, angle of attack %s degrees, wing area 10 m², air density 1.225 kg/m³.
command.aerocore.sample.output: Lift %s N | Drag %s N | Dynamic pressure %s Pa | %s

entity.aerocore.physics_probe.label: AeroCore probe · %s kg

command.aerocore.platform.none: No platform owned by you within 32 blocks.
command.aerocore.platform.blocked: The platform's envelope is obstructed, outside the world border, or in unloaded chunks. Use open, deep water and leave room for the ballast.

command.aerocore.platform.changed: Platform reconfigured; motion reset. Ballast/tilt edits are external test adjustments, not a simulated actuator.
command.aerocore.platform.cleared: Removed %s platforms owned by you within 64 blocks.
command.aerocore.platform.debug.changed: Display: %s. Forces: red weight, cyan buoyancy, yellow drag, magenta contact, orange thrust, lavender added mass and wave inertia, dark teal wave radiation, blue lift (hull trailing edge, rudder), green net (1 m = 1000 N; capped at 3 m). Flow: white air, blue water (1 m = 4 m/s; capped at 1 m); light-blue dots mark the sampled wave surface. Ambient samples, not CFD wakes; only visible to you.
command.aerocore.platform.debug.legend: F: red weight / cyan buoyancy / yellow drag / magenta contact / orange thrust / lavender inertia / dark teal radiation / blue lift / green net | %s flow: white air / blue water | %s C

command.aerocore.waves.environment: Wind %s m/s at 10 m toward %s deg, with gusts | coast: %s
command.aerocore.waves.coast.none: not surveyed (open-sea waves everywhere; /aerocore waves survey)
command.aerocore.waves.coast.ready: %s of %s survey points on land; waves refract, shoal, are sheltered and break over the surveyed bed
command.aerocore.waves.coast.failed: the survey could not be used; open-sea waves
command.aerocore.waves.no_region: No wave region contains this position.
command.aerocore.waves.wind_set: Wind over the wave region: %s m/s at 10 m, blowing toward %s deg, with gusts. It sets the whitecaps, drifts the surface water and pushes boats and bodies; the waves stay as they are (windsea raises a sea from a wind; wind weather makes it follow the weather).
command.aerocore.waves.surveyed: Surveyed the bed under the wave region: %s x %s points every %s m, %s of them on land. The coastal waves are being computed (about a second).
command.aerocore.waves.wind_sea: Wind sea: U10 %s m/s. Fetch over this water, straight upwind to the shore (median over the region): %s m, plus %s beyond the surveyed square. The sea for that fetch: Hs %s m, Tp %s s (JONSWAP growth, held at the breaking steepness for short fetch); each spot grows with its own fetch, from about Hs %s m near the upwind shore to %s m downwind.
command.aerocore.waves.wind_sea_too_high: This wind raises Hs %s m over that fetch, more than the 4 m the sea commands allow; give a shorter fetch.
command.aerocore.waves.survey_cleared: Removed the bed survey: this region's waves are the open-sea waves everywhere again (no refraction, shelter, surf or fetch growth). /aerocore waves survey measures it again.
command.aerocore.waves.environment_weath: Wind follows the weather: clear %s, rain %s, thunder %s m/s at 10 m (now %s m/s) toward %s deg, with gusts | coast: %s
command.aerocore.waves.wind_weather_set: Wind over the wave region now follows the weather: %s m/s in clear weather, %s m/s in rain, %s m/s in thunderstorms (at 10 m, blowing toward %s deg; now %s m/s), changing smoothly as the weather does. Minecraft's weather has no wind, so these speeds are a rule (defaults from the Beaufort scale). Gusts ride on the mean wind; the waves stay as they are.
command.aerocore.waves.sea_state: Sea now at %s%% of its synthesised height (Hs %s m); it grows and calms with the wind over time.
command.aerocore.wind.info: World wind (%s): reference 10 m wind over open terrain %s m/s, blowing toward %s°. Here: %s m above the ground or water, upwind effective roughness %s m, canopy %s m; mean wind %s m/s (hill speed-up %s%%, %s%% left after shelter), gust now %s m/s.
command.aerocore.wind.weather: following the weather and synoptic changes
command.aerocore.wind.set: World wind fixed at %s m/s at 10 m over open terrain, blowing toward %s°. Terrain, forests, water and height still shape the wind everywhere; /aerocore wind natural returns it to the weather.
command.aerocore.wind.natural: World wind follows the weather again: clear 5, rain 10, thunder 15 m/s (Minecraft's weather has no wind; this is a rule), times slow synoptic changes over several Minecraft days; now %s m/s toward %s°.
command.aerocore.waves.natural_on: Natural seas on: open water at the sea level near players gets waves from the world wind by itself (regions up to 128 m around players, following them, clear of commanded regions; ponds get short chop, the ocean long waves, their height following the wind).
command.aerocore.waves.natural_off: Natural seas off: the natural regions are removed; commanded regions stay.
command.aerocore.ground.firm: Ground here: %s (firm). Tyre peak friction %s (Magic Formula), rolling resistance coefficient %s (for a car wheel: 4 kN load, 0.65 m diameter, 0.2 m width).
command.aerocore.ground.soft: Ground here: %s (soft; Bekker-Wong soil). Tyre peak friction %s; a car wheel (4 kN, 0.65 m diameter, 0.2 m width) sinks %s cm, rolling resistance coefficient %s, and the soil gives at most %s times the load in traction.
